axisScale.meaning: Corpus-relative axis position; higher is always more desirable. 50 is typical across measured sources, with positions derived from adjusted z-scores and bounded for display.

bands.label: Strongest measured headline value
bands.summary: Headlines most often combine concrete information with comparatively restrained packaging.

bands.label: Above-typical measured headline value
bands.summary: Headlines are usually informative or restrained, with some weaker axes or mixed behaviour.

bands.label: Below-typical measured headline value
bands.summary: Headlines more often omit concrete anchors or use more attention-oriented framing.

bands.label: Weakest measured headline value
bands.summary: Headlines are comparatively thin on concrete information, heavier on packaging, or both.

axes.label: Events & actions
axes.description: The headline says something happened, changed or was decided.

axes.label: Numbers & detail
axes.description: The headline carries concrete quantities, amounts or counts.

axes.label: Time & place
axes.description: The headline anchors the story in a time or location.

axes.label: Cause & effect
axes.description: The headline links events, causes or consequences.

axes.label: Real-world stakes
axes.description: The headline signals costs, risks, harm, benefit or other material consequences.

axes.label: Evidence cues
axes.description: The headline points to research, documents, data or other evidence.

axes.label: Context & comparison
axes.description: The headline compares, contrasts or places events in a sequence.

axes.label: Explanatory framing
axes.description: The headline offers explanation, mechanism, guidance or service information.

axes.label: Curiosity restraint
axes.description: The headline avoids stock teasers and withholding the point.

axes.label: Low search-capture packaging
axes.description: The headline avoids direct-address, how-to and search-capture packaging.

axes.label: Sensational restraint
axes.description: The headline avoids sensational vocabulary and celebrity/personal-life framing.

profile.ownership: Tweak Town Pty Ltd — founder Cameron Wilmot is still managing director; independent, no media-group owner, Australian company based in Victoria.
profile.model: Ads plus optional ad-free subscriptions introduced in 2024-25, explicitly framed as supporting independent tech journalism.
profile.history: Began in 1997 as 'Wilmot's Website', a teenage homepage; renamed TweakTown in 1999 after a viral 56k-modem tweaking guide. Grew from one-man hardware tweaking guides into an international reviews operation.

sources.label: PsyPost

profile.ownership: PsyPost Media Inc., an S-corporation in Roseville, California — owned and edited by founder Eric W. Dolan, who started it as a college project in 2010. No university, publisher or advocacy affiliation.
profile.model: Display ads plus premium subscriptions. States it takes no money from researchers, universities or PR firms for coverage.
profile.history: Founded 2010; has covered 15,000+ peer-reviewed studies with a self-conscious mission to avoid the genre's failures — implied causality, missing sample sizes, glossed-over measurement.

notes: PsyPost often writes formulaic research-claim headlines. That raises evidence and causal scores without establishing independent verification of the studies.

profile.history: Eurogamer grew out of Gamer Network and was sold by ReedPop to Ziff Davis’s IGN Entertainment in 2024.

profile.leaning: Broadly liberal/left-of-centre opinion culture; ownership is designed to protect editorial independence rather than enforce a party line.

profile.ownership: Jerusalem Post Group, controlled since 2004 by Eli Azur's Mirkaei Tikshoret — bought for $13.3m from Conrad Black's collapsing Hollinger empire after a bitter arbitration battle that shut out Canada's CanWest. Azur also owns Maariv.
profile.leaning: Centrist-to-right Israeli establishment paper, aimed heavily at the diaspora and international readers; columnists span the spectrum but the editorial line is security-hawkish.
profile.history: Founded 1932 by Gershon Agron as The Palestine Post under the British Mandate; renamed in 1950. Supported Labor until 1989, then shifted sharply right under Conrad Black's ownership (Bret Stephens edited it 2002-04), before moving partly back to centre under Azur.

profile.ownership: Flagship site of The Multimedia Group — Ghana's largest independent commercial media company. Majority shareholder is founder Kwasi Twum with 92.5%; notably, the state-owned Ghana Broadcasting Corporation holds 7.5%.
profile.leaning: Commercially independent but establishment-oriented; middle-to-upper-income audience positioning from its Joy FM origins.
profile.history: Grew out of Joy 99.7 FM (1995), Ghana's first private English-language radio station; the site launched 1996 as the first Ghana-based news site streaming live radio. The group expanded by acquisition into six radio stations, three TV channels (Joy News, Joy Prime, Adom TV) and MultiTV.

profile.ownership: WCCF TECH Inc. — founder Abdullah Saad is CEO and editor-in-chief. Privately held, bootstrapped; editorial operations Vancouver, legal entity reported as Dubai-domiciled.
profile.leaning: Enthusiast-native voice with heavy rumor/leak coverage — faster and looser than mainstream tech press.
profile.history: Started 2004 as a small tech-enthusiast forum ('Where Consumers Come First'); grew into a top-five most-commented tech site covering PC hardware, semiconductors and gaming.

sources.label: Medical Xpress

profile.ownership: Science X network — wholly owned by Omicron Technology Limited, headquartered in Douglas, Isle of Man. Founded 2004 by two PhD students; Medical Xpress spun out of Phys.org's medical channel in 2011.
profile.model: Advertising-funded (plus voluntary donations). Network publishes 200+ articles daily — a high-volume mix of in-house reports and editor-processed university press releases, which the network insists are hand-curated rather than republished, though external assessors describe much of it as churnalism with straight press-release structure.
profile.leaning: Pro-science, no political agenda — Media Bias/Fact Check rates it High for factual reporting with a clean fact-check record.

notes: High evidence and causal scores partly reflect research-release phrasing. They do not by themselves show independent verification of the underlying studies.

profile.ownership: Published by Dar Al-Watan/Qatar Information & Marketing — majority-owned through its publisher by Hamad bin Jassim Al Thani, Qatar's former prime minister and foreign minister, a senior royal and cousin of the emir. Chairman is Sheikh Hamad bin Suhaim Al Thani.
profile.leaning: Pro-government per documented assessments — Qatar is an absolute monarchy whose media operates within royal red lines; read as the semi-official English window.
profile.history: Launched 2006 as Qatar's third English daily, sister to the Arabic Al-Watan, targeting the country's large expat population.

profile.leaning: Market- and institution-oriented rather than a conventional party tabloid; elite business access is both strength and blind spot.

sources.label: Reddit
notes: Reddit rows reflect headlines as posted or repeated on the platform. They describe reused headline text, not original reporting or verification by Reddit.

profile.leaning: Pro-business and founder-described pro-libertarian ownership context; it should not be flattened into a generic right-wing tabloid.

sources.label: ScienceAlert
notes: Popular science rewriting can make research cues prominent; the score does not assess the quality of the underlying paper.

profile.ownership: Owned by Dongwha Enterprise, a wood-based manufacturing conglomerate, which also owns the Korean-language Hankook Ilbo — acquired together after the Hankook Ilbo Media Group collapsed in a 2013-14 embezzlement scandal (chairman Chang Jae-ku imprisoned for embezzling 45.6bn won).
profile.leaning: Centrist, establishment-aligned; fiscal conservative / culturally liberal per its sister paper's positioning. Read as an establishment window into Korea rather than an independent voice.
profile.history: South Korea's oldest active English-language daily, founded Nov 1950 mid-Korean War by educator Helen Kim to publicise the war effort abroad. Famously evacuated Seoul by the last train in 1951 and published handwritten headlines from Busan. Criticised Syngman Rhee's dictatorship despite close early ties.

sources.label: Seeking Alpha
notes: Earnings, transcript and market-data formats make this source narrower than a general news publisher; read the axes before the composite.

profile.leaning: London-focused establishment/free-sheet identity; political line has changed over time and should be tracked at article level.

sources.label: New York Post / Page Six

profile.kind: US tabloid newspaper and digital publisher
profile.leaning: Conservative tabloid sensibility; hard-news coverage, commentary, front-page framing and Page Six celebrity reporting have different evidentiary profiles.

notes: Page Six is measured with the New York Post because it belongs to the same publishing operation; the combined view is dominated by the larger New York Post stream.

profile.ownership: Independent Digital News & Media. Largest shareholder Evgeny Lebedev (~47%), son of a former KGB oligarch, made a peer in 2020. Investor Justin Byam Shaw holds ~20%. A 30% stake sold in 2017 to offshore companies fronted by Saudi businessman Sultan Mohamed Abuljadayel — described in court by the UK government as part-owned by the Saudi state via 'unconventional, complex and clandestine' deals.
profile.leaning: Centrist to centre-left editorially, but ownership structure is the key context: Saudi-linked minority stake since 2017, with a formal editorial-independence agreement whose enforcement is opaque.
profile.history: Founded 1986 as a print national positioned between the broadsheets; first UK national to go digital-only (2016). Now profitable online, with licensed offshoots including Independent Arabia.

profile.ownership: Published by Associated Newspapers (DMGT — the Daily Mail's parent, controlled by Lord Rothermere's family trust). It is the money section of MailOnline, not an independent title: its journalists double as Daily Mail, Money Mail and Financial Mail on Sunday staff.
profile.leaning: Consumer-championing personal finance with the Mail's editorial gravity underneath — campaigny, reader-service oriented, small-c conservative instincts on tax and property.
profile.history: Grew out of the Mail's money pages into what DMGT calls the UK's biggest financial website; its podcast ran ten years by 2024.

sources.label: Mashable
notes: Regional Mashable editions are grouped because they substantially reuse the same articles; their measured headline profiles are broadly similar rather than dominated by one outlier edition.

profile.leaning: Institutionally required to be impartial; criticised from both left and right over framing, access, and political coverage.

profile.ownership: Kasturi & Sons Ltd, wholly owned by descendants of Kasturi Ranga Iyengar, who bought the paper in 1905. Family members occupy the board and editorships — N. Ram (great-grandson of the buyer) chairs the publishing arm. Publishing demerged into THG Publishing (52% KSL) in 2017.
profile.leaning: Centre-left, secular, establishment-liberal; historically close to India's intellectual left (N. Ram's own politics lean that way) while remaining the south's paper of record.
profile.history: Founded 1878 in Chennai as a weekly by six young nationalists with 'a rupee and three-quarters' of capital — a paper of the freedom struggle. Gandhi unveiled a portrait at its offices in 1923. Became a morning daily in 1940; launched India's first newspaper website in 1996. A family schism over the editorship played out publicly in 2011-12.

profile.ownership: New Straits Times Press, part of the Media Prima conglomerate — Malaysia's largest media group (TV3, Berita Harian, Harian Metro). Media Prima's lineage runs directly through UMNO, the party that ruled Malaysia for six decades: the paper was seized into UMNO's Fleet Holdings in 1972 and passed through Renong and MRCB before Media Prima's formation.
profile.leaning: Historically the English-language voice of the UMNO establishment; post-2018 change of government loosened but did not sever its establishment alignment.
profile.history: Born of the 1965 Singapore split — when The Straits Times' KL operations became untenable, UMNO vice-president Tengku Razaleigh bought the Malaysian arm at the PM's request in 1972; renamed New Straits Times in 1974. Control of the paper was a instrument in UMNO factional politics for decades (Mahathir vs Razaleigh, then Anwar's camp).

profile.ownership: MarketBeat Media LLC, owned by founder Matt Paulson of Sioux Falls, South Dakota — built from a personal-finance blog he started in a college dorm in 2006. No media-group parent.
profile.model: Subscriptions ('All Access'), advertising — and aggressive email-list growth: BuzzFeed reported in 2020 that MarketBeat paid junk-news 'McGorty' sites for affiliate signups.
profile.history: Incorporated 2011 as Analyst Ratings Network, rebranded MarketBeat 2015. Compiles analyst ratings, insider trades, dividends and SEC filings into newsletter-driven content; much of its market news is republished Associated Press wire copy.

profile.ownership: Future plc — launched in-house by Future in 2008, not acquired. Future is a London-listed specialist-media giant running ~175 brands, monetised through ads, magazines, and above all affiliate commerce (~33% of group revenue is eCommerce commission).
profile.model: Future's commerce engine ('Hawk') powers buying guides, deals and coupon content — affiliate fees are the business model, openly disclosed. Editorial claims no payment for reviews and independently chosen products.
profile.history: Launched 2008 as the UK's biggest consumer tech site; expanded to US 2012, Australia 2012. Claims 16,000+ reviewed products and 30m+ readers.

profile.ownership: Future plc since March 2019, when Future bought parent Mobile Nations ($55m+ upfront) — alongside Android Central and iMore. London-listed Future is one of the largest specialist-media groups (TechRadar, PC Gamer, Tom's Guide).
profile.model: Future's commerce-driven specialist-media model: audience monetised through affiliate buying guides and ads against enthusiast coverage.
profile.history: Started as forums and a mini-blog by Dieter Bohn (later of The Verge) in 2006; relaunched as WMExperts in 2009 covering Windows Mobile, became WPCentral then Windows Central as Microsoft's platform shifted from phones to Windows/Xbox/Surface.

sources.label: Phys.org

profile.kind: High-volume science and research news portal
profile.model: Science X says it is not a blind press-release service and that staff select, edit and fact-check material. Even accepting that self-description, the output is a high-volume mix whose provenance varies article by article: staff reporting, licensed copy and university or journal press material.

notes: Research-release phrasing can raise evidence and causal scores. Treat them as evidence of dense research claims, not proof of independent scientific scrutiny.

profile.ownership: Wholly owned by a holding company whose shareholders are mostly non-profits and trusts — largest is Inkululeko South Africa Media; no shareholder exceeds 50%. Explicitly no billionaire owner, no media group, party or religious affiliation.
profile.model: Hybrid funding: reader membership (voluntary, no paywall), advertising, events, and philanthropy — Open Society Foundation, Donald Gordon, Claude Leon, Millennium Trust among disclosed grantors; no single donor over 5% of income.
profile.history: Founded 2009 by Branko Brkic and Styli Charalambous after Brkic's print magazines folded — five people on plastic chairs on a stoep. Its Marikana massacre reporting (2012), contradicting official accounts, established its reputation; grew to 14.5m unique browsers in the 2024 election month.

sources.label: Xbox Wire
notes: Xbox Wire is official platform communication, so its score is not a measure of independent games journalism.

profile.ownership: Notebookcheck Publishing GmbH — 100% privately owned by its three Austrian founders (Klaus A. Hinum, Stefan Hinum, J. Simon Leitner), no outside investors or media group.
profile.model: Funded by ads, advertorials and affiliate links (Amazon, Tradedoubler, Awin). Review units are loaned by manufacturers or bought editorially; their transparency page states lenders get no preview and no influence.
profile.history: Founded 2005 as a student hobby project after the founders couldn't find proper laptop reviews; became a business in 2007 and grew into one of the largest laptop/mobile review operations, publishing in 10+ languages with a database of tens of thousands of reviews.

profile.ownership: Publicly owned — a statutory corporation funded by the Australian government budget, advertising-free by statute since 1932.
profile.history: Launched 1932 as a single radio service; now Australia's most trusted news provider and largest scripted-content producer. Its emergency bushfire and COVID coverage drove record audiences.

profile.ownership: Business Recorder Group, 100% owned by the Zuberi family — son Shahab and grandsons (Wamiq, Asif, Arshad, Ahmad Zuberi) run operations. The group also owns Aaj News TV, Aaj Entertainment, Play TV, security-printing and IT interests.
profile.leaning: Pro-business establishment paper; family-run with the founder's son as editor, so ownership and editorial voice are fused.
profile.history: Founded 1965 by M.A. Zuberi, who was hired by Mohammad Ali Jinnah himself as an apprentice at Dawn in 1945. Claims to be the Muslim world's first daily dedicated to economics and finance — the pioneer of business journalism in Pakistan.

sources.label: Mirror

profile.leaning: Historically the clearest Labour-aligned UK national tabloid, though modern Reach content mixes politics, service, celebrity, and syndicated local copy.

notes: Sensational and personal framing is the largest negative contribution here, even where individual headlines are otherwise concrete.

profile.ownership: Paramount, a Skydance Corporation — controlled by David Ellison (son of Oracle billionaire Larry Ellison) after the $8bn Skydance-Paramount merger cleared the FCC in 2025. In October 2025 Paramount bought Bari Weiss's The Free Press (~$150m) and installed Weiss as CBS News editor-in-chief, reporting directly to Ellison.
profile.history: One of the three legacy US broadcast news divisions — the network of Murrow and Cronkite. Long rated third of the big three; the Skydance merger came with commitments to the Trump administration's FCC on 'diversity of viewpoints', and Weiss's appointment — an anti-woke opinion entrepreneur with no broadcast background — was explicitly aimed at appealing to right-of-center viewers.

profile.leaning: Independent watchdog identity with a history of pressure from military regimes; “leftist” labels are useful only in Nigerian political context.

sources.label: Nature

profile.kind: Scientific journal and editorially independent science news portal

notes: The low event/action score is largely a form effect: many Nature rows are journal article titles written as descriptive noun phrases. This does not mean the underlying research articles lack evidence.

profile.ownership: DMG Media — same DMGT stable as the Daily Mail, wholly owned since 2022 by Lord Rothermere's Rothermere Continuation Limited after delisting from the stock exchange.
profile.leaning: Deliberately non-partisan — unlike its conservative sister the Mail, Metro has never endorsed a party. The reader-service neutral register is a product decision for a mass commute audience.
profile.history: Launched March 1999 after DMGT executives scouted the Swedish Metro concept; became the UK's most-circulated paper in 2018 (overtaking The Sun) through station and bus distribution, reaching ~5m readers daily.

sources.label: OregonLive obituaries
notes: This measurement mostly describes syndicated obituary entries rather than OregonLive’s wider newsroom output.

sources.label: Inquirer
notes: Inquirer verticals and regional subdomains are grouped as sections of one publisher. Some verticals are very small and differ in style, so the combined view mainly describes the main and news streams.

sources.label: Handelsblatt

profile.ownership: Handelsblatt Media Group, wholly owned by DvH Medien GmbH — Dieter von Holtzbrinck's family holding, which also owns the Berliner Tagesspiegel outright and 50% of ZEIT-Verlag. Family-owned since 1971.
profile.leaning: Pro-market, ordoliberal establishment economics voice — the paper of record for German business. Editorially independent tradition but unashamedly the perspective of capital.
profile.history: Founded 1946 in Düsseldorf as Germany's post-war business paper; became the flagship of the country's leading economics media house, adding WirtschaftsWoche and a large specialist publishing operation.

notes: English-language cue detection undercounts German-language headlines; treat this position as non-comparable with English-language sources.

sources.label: New Scientist
notes: The low evidence score often means the headline avoids formulaic “study finds” phrasing; it is not evidence that the article lacks research support.

sources.label: Kotaku

profile.history: Kotaku moved from the former Gawker/G/O ecosystem to Swiss publisher Keleops, the same group that had acquired Gizmodo.

notes: The low position mainly reflects fewer time/place anchors, less causal/consequence language, and more direct-address packaging.

sources.label: Daily Mail

profile.leaning: Commonly described as right-leaning and socially conservative; the Mail on Sunday has historically taken some different positions.

notes: The low position is driven especially by sensational and personal framing, alongside weaker time/place and evidence cues.
